pr.title: Windows builds and renders: the CLI, the paths, and the daemon (windows-portability.md chunk 2)
pr.head: bd26b8a1b40d2b578a8e3cd2e70747dac51320af

summary: field is a command-line tool that keeps a music project as files in Git. Its audio engine is a C++ daemon, field-audiod. The CLI runs it two ways: as a subprocess that renders one file and exits (--render, --render-live, --scan), and as a long-lived server it talks to over a local control socket for playback and recording. The Windows portability plan, docs/projects/windows-portability/readme.md, brings field up on Windows in five chunks. This pull request is chunk 2. Its base is #158, which sits on chunk 1 (#157), and #161 and #163 build on it.

Chunk 2 makes field build on Windows and makes the subprocess half of the daemon work there, so offline rendering runs. The control socket stays POSIX-only until chunk 4 replaces it with a Windows named pipe. Until then, the daemon's serve mode refuses on Windows, and every test that needs the socket skips there with a comment that names what will remove the guard.

1. Paths become data with one spelling. On Windows, Node's relative() answers with backslashes, so a song directory came out as songs\creek. Build labels are made from that directory, so no label a user typed could ever match. Project-relative paths that the program compares or sends now always use /.
  2. MSVC compiles the daemon. Five fixes: std::numbers::pi for the non-standard M_PI, an explicitly move-only LiveSession::Track, a guarded SIGPIPE, a Windows stub for the socket server, and Windows spellings of fsync and ftruncate in the recording code.
  3. The CLI finds and builds the binary. daemonBinary() adds .exe on Windows, and pnpm build:native passes --config Release, which Visual Studio's multi-config build needs.
  4. The tests know which platform they are on. Suffix assertions compare in the platform separator, the stub worker runs through Node itself, and socket-bound tests skip on win32.

Nobody has built this exact head on Windows. The author's Windows run was at 1acb58f on 2026-08-18. Since then, a merge of the base branch brought in the recording code from main (#166, #167, #169, #170). Later commits port that code's one POSIX-only file, capture.cpp, and guard its three socket test files on win32. The review of this head is clean, with no finding open, so a human approval is what remains. The review body lists four non-blocking suggestions.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Serve mode: the daemon running as a server on the control socket, for playback and recording.
  • Subprocess mode: the daemon run once with --render, --render-live, or --scan, with no socket.
  • Project-relative path: a path from the project root, such as songs/creek/tracks/pad.yaml.
  • Multi-config generator: a CMake build, such as Visual Studio's, that picks Debug or Release at build time with --config, not at configure time.
  • Chunk 4: the plan's named-pipe transport, which replaces the Unix socket on Windows.

groups.title: Project-relative paths use forward slashes
groups.kicker: The model, the build report, and the live session spell every project-relative path with /
intro: A project-relative path is a path from the project root, such as songs/creek. The model loads every song and file with a path like this. Build labels such as //songs/creek/track:pad are made from a song's directory, and the YAML schemas already reject \ in paths. On Windows, Node's relative() answers with backslashes, so the model stored songs\creek, and no label or pattern a user typed could match it. The author reports about 70 tests failing with "no such label" for this reason.

The fix states one rule: a project-relative path that the program compares, stores, or sends uses /. A path that stays local, such as an absolute output path, keeps the platform's separator. On macOS and Linux the separator is already /, so nothing changes there.

Three places apply the rule. projectPath in the model converts each loaded file path and each song directory, and compileSession calls it for the input file paths it writes into the session JSON for the daemon. projectRelative in the build command converts the paths that field build prints. The two diagnostics for a stranded takes file are built as slash-joined strings.

checks.text: Every comparison against song.dir in src/ already compares a slash-joined value: traced the s.dir === sites in transport.ts, land.ts, and graph/build.ts, and every caller of musicalContext. Each passes a label package, songs/${name}, songDirOfPkg, songDirOfPath, or a graph node's songDir, and all of these use /.

files.note: Exports projectPath, uses it for each loaded file's path and each song's directory, and slash-joins the two stranded-takes diagnostics.
projectRelative returns a slash-separated path when the path is inside the project. Both callers print it.

checks.text: Both callers of projectRelative print its output. The plan's chunk 2 amendment counts that output as data, while §7.4 says a printed path keeps the platform's separator. The review suggests saying in one place that these printed paths take slashes, and why.

files.note: The session JSON's file paths come from projectPath.

checks.text: The daemon resolves these paths with projectRoot.getChildFile (live.cpp:107), and JUCE's File::getChildFile replaces / with \ on Windows before it joins. Checked in the fetched JUCE source, juce_File.cpp:439.
With relative and sep dropped from the imports, nothing else in the file uses them. Checked by searching the file at this head.

groups.title: MSVC compiles the daemon
groups.kicker: Five fixes that let Visual Studio's compiler build field-audiod, with no change to what it renders
intro: field-audiod is the C++ audio daemon. GCC and Clang build it on Linux and macOS. MSVC, Microsoft's compiler, rejected it for reasons that reading the code had not found. The fixes keep behavior identical on the other platforms.

1. M_PI becomes std::numbers::pi. M_PI is not standard C++. glibc and Apple's library define it, and MSVC does not. std::numbers::pi is the same double, so renders do not change. The daemon builds as C++20, which <numbers> needs.
  2. LiveSession::Track is explicitly move-only. A track holds unique_ptrs in its effect chain, so copying one cannot compile. MSVC instantiated the copy anyway when a vector of tracks grew.
  3. SIGPIPE is guarded. Windows has no SIGPIPE. A write to a closed pipe returns an error there, so the guarantee the POSIX line gives holds without it.
  4. The socket server has a Windows stub. server.cpp is hand-written AF_UNIX code. On Windows it compiles to a stub whose start() refuses with a pointer to chunk 4, so serve mode exits while the subprocess modes run.
  5. capture.cpp spells fsync and ftruncate per platform. The recording code came in with the base merge. MSVC has _commit and _chsize_s in their place.

checks.text: The Linux CI job built the daemon with GCC and passed at 18849a0. Since then the only daemon change is a comment in live.h. No compiler has built this head on Windows.

files.note: Wraps the POSIX server in #if and adds a Windows stub whose start() refuses.

checks.text: The stub defines every non-inline public member that server.h declares: the constructor, the destructor, start, beginShutdown, broadcast, sweepClosedConnections, and connectionCount. The helpers in the POSIX half sit in an anonymous namespace, so nothing outside the file needs them. Checked by reading both files.

files.note: Guards the SIGPIPE line on _WIN32 and amends its comment to say why Windows needs no equivalent.
Declares Track's special members: copy deleted, move defaulted.

checks.text: The comment names the trigger: MSVC's std::map move constructor is not noexcept, so vector growth falls back through move_if_noexcept to a copy, which cannot copy the chain.

files.note: Adds syncToDisk and truncateTo, which use _commit and _chsize_s on Windows and fsync and ftruncate elsewhere.

checks.text: Both helpers sit in the file's anonymous namespace, and the two fopen calls they serve use binary modes (r+b, wb), so MSVC's text mode cannot rewrite audio bytes. Checked by reading the file at this head.

Recording runs only in serve mode, which refuses on Windows until chunk 4. So this code compiles on Windows but does not run there yet. The review suggests opening these files, and the WAV files in wavfile.cpp, through a UTF-8 std::filesystem::path. MSVC reads a narrow path in the ANSI code page, so a non-ASCII path fails to open.

files.note: Two uses of M_PI become std::numbers::pi.
Two uses of M_PI in the pan law become std::numbers::pi.
Two uses of M_PI in the resampler's filter design become std::numbers::pi.

groups.title: The CLI finds and builds the binary
groups.kicker: The .exe suffix in daemonBinary() and --config Release in build:native
intro: daemonBinary() is the one function the CLI and the tests use to find the built daemon. It looks in the JUCE artefacts directory, native/audiod/build/field-audiod_artefacts/Release/. On Windows the file is field-audiod.exe, so the function now adds that suffix.

The directory name depends on the build configuration. Visual Studio's build is multi-config: it ignores -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release and builds Debug unless cmake --build gets --config Release. Generators that build one configuration ignore that flag, so build:native now passes it on every platform, beside the --parallel 4 that #165 added.
Finding the binary on Windows also turns on every test that skips only when the binary is missing. Each such test that dials the socket now skips on win32 as well.

files.note: daemonBinary() adds .exe on win32.

checks.text: Every test file that reaches the daemon socket guards those tests on win32: audiod/client, live-session, plugin-hosting, play-daemon, click-daemon, punch-daemon, record-daemon, and version. Checked by listing every test file that calls AudiodClient, playThroughDaemon, playLiveSession, recordTake, or transportCommand, then reading its guards.

files.note: build:native passes --config Release after --parallel 4.

groups.title: The stub worker runs through Node
groups.kicker: A JavaScript interpreter override starts with process.execPath instead of its shebang
intro: field's generative workers are Python daemons. An environment variable such as FIELD_ACED_PYTHON overrides the interpreter that starts them. The tests point it at src/testing/stub-worker.mjs, a stub that answers like a worker. On macOS and Linux the stub ran through its #! line. Windows has no shebang support, and starting the file fails with EFTYPE.

workerLaunchCommand now starts a .js or .mjs override with process.execPath, the Node binary that is running field. That works the same on every platform. On Windows the stub tests still skip, because the stub listens on an AF_UNIX socket.

files.note: Starts a .js or .mjs interpreter override with process.execPath.
The test helper builds .venv/Scripts on Windows, which is the directory workerScriptInstalled checks there.

groups.title: Tests skip what Windows cannot run yet, and compare in its separator
groups.kicker: Per-test guards with their reasons, and suffix checks written with sep
intro: The tests change in two ways. Assertions that compared a native absolute path with a /-joined literal now build the literal with join or sep. Tests that need something Windows does not have yet skip on win32, each with a comment that names what will remove the guard. The overview's table lists the guard families.
One more test fix: plan-limits.test.ts runs pnpm gen:limits. On Windows pnpm is a .cmd script, which Node starts only through a shell, so the test passes shell on win32.

checks.text: The guard counts match the plan's amendment: 9 guards in version.test.ts, 21 in generate.test.ts, 3 describes in aced and voiced, and 2 in graph/build.test.ts. Counted in the diff.

groups.title: The plan records what chunk 2 found
groups.kicker: Three dated amendments to chunk 2 in the Windows portability plan
intro: The plan's §5 lists the chunks. This change adds three amendments under chunk 2. The first, dated 2026-08-17, records the path finding, the smaller Windows fixes, and the guard families. The second, dated 2026-08-18, records what MSVC found and the author's Windows run: every test file passed, and the block-invariance check reported bit-identical output. The third, dated 2026-10-10, records the recording code the base merge brought in: the capture.cpp port and the guards on its three socket test files.

§7.1 now lists every guard whose comment names chunk 4 as chunk 4's to remove. The plan stays in-progress, and the amendments add no open question. Other edits in this region of the file, such as §6's 104-byte answer and §7.4's statement of the slash rule, come from the base branch, not this pull request.

files.note: Adds three chunk 2 amendments to §5 and widens §7.1's list of guards chunk 4 removes.

checks.text: This amendment lists diagnostics and projectRelative's output as data, but both are printed for a person, and §7.4 says a printed path keeps the platform's separator. The review suggests reconciling the two.
